trust_decision.summary: parseIndex decides a line is a ---/+++ file header (and stops metadata parsing) with /^(---|\+\+\+|@@)\s/, but parseFileHeader only consumes it if /^(---|\+\+\+)\s+(.*)\r?$/ matches; a header containing a non-trailing \r, \u2028 or \u2029 passes the first test and fails the second, so nothing is consumed, the hunk loop breaks on ---\s, and the outer while loop in parsePatch pushes empty index objects forever (memory-growing infinite loop).

landing_point.why: Advisory names parsePatch and the previous ReDoS fix (#647) already reworked header regexes in this file; the only header regex with a .* capture is parseFileHeader's.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API parsePatch(uniDiff) (src/index.ts:103); also reached via applyPatch(source, string) at src/patch/apply.ts:61 and applyPatches(string, opts) at src/patch/apply.ts:341

O3_reason_to_dismiss: None real: applyPatch/applyPatches just delegate to parsePatch, so a fix in parseFileHeader (or a progress guard in the parsePatch loop) covers every route at once.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Header parsing must keep stripping a trailing \r on CRLF patches, splitting off the tab-separated timestamp header, unquoting "quoted" filenames and unescaping \\; an over-broad fix that throws on any header with \r or line-separator chars, or rejects unknown lines, breaks CRLF patches and filenames with odd characters.
